title.ja: 記おくカードびじゅつかん

synopsis: Stasi turns her wall of hand-drawn kanji cards into a little flashcard program, and her funniest card reads 味 as a mouth with a tree in it. Tom's speed round races past the truth and Shin's component evidence shows the part is 未, not 木. The learner rebuilds the card as a program that keeps Stasi's vivid picture while a button reveals the real part, and Tom redesigns his game so fast can still be right.

scenes.goal: Meet Stasi through her card museum and her funniest card, and hit the moment the joke turns out to name the wrong component.
scenes.dramaticQuestion: Can the class correct a memorable card without turning it into a plain one?
scenes.learnerNeed: A revision task where component evidence has to change a kanji claim while the vivid picture is protected.

nodes.description: The classroom's side board has become a small museum: rows of hand-drawn kanji memory cards pinned in a grid, each with its own picture. In front of one card — 味, drawn as a wide-open mouth clamped over a leafy branch — a small knot of people has gathered. The projector shows an empty flashcard shell, waiting to be filled.

nodes.intent: Welcome the class to her card museum, show off her favorite card's vivid mouth-and-tree picture, and say she wants to turn the whole wall into a flashcard program.
nodes.attentionTarget: the 味 card and the empty program shell on the projector

nodes.intent: Turn the wall into a fast speed round, race to name the parts, and confidently blurt the wrong component before moving on.
nodes.attentionTarget: the timer and the next card, not the strokes he just named

nodes.intent: Stop the race, decompose the character by its actual strokes, and show the part is 未 (not 木) — carrying both a meaning and the reading.
nodes.attentionTarget: the extra top stroke that separates 未 from 木

nodes.description: On the projector the two shapes sit side by side, 木 and 未, with the extra top stroke of 未 circled. Below them the empty program shell now shows a single labelled control: a part button marked ぶひん, waiting for what it should reveal.

nodes.resume: The false part is exposed and the picture is still on the wall. The learner steps in to rebuild the card as a program that keeps the image and reveals the true part.

nodes.resumeContext: Component evidence says the part is 未, not 木. The learner describes the flashcard program they want, states the button condition (press the part button and the true component appears), and states the changed plan aloud: keep Stasi's picture, correct the part.

nodes.description: Only the sentence about the button and the changed part returns for another pass. The picture and the earlier welcome stay exactly where they were.

nodes.resume: The program is described: picture kept, button reveals the real part. Stasi looks at the draft the class has built from her card.

scenes.goal: Let Stasi rebuild her card so it stays vivid and becomes accurate, and let Tom's speed cost land as a redesigned game rather than a scolding.
scenes.dramaticQuestion: Can accuracy and expression share the same card, and can a fast challenge hold both?
scenes.learnerNeed: A stance choice about how to back a corrected card and a challenge that outran itself.

nodes.description: On the projector the revised card draft has appeared: the same wide-open mouth, but now clamped over a hard green fruit, with 未 labelled beside it and the ぶひん button sitting underneath, ready to press.

nodes.intent: Take the correction and rebuild the card in her own vivid style — dropping the tree, keeping the mouth, and making 未 into a picture of tasting something not yet ripe.
nodes.attentionTarget: the mouth-and-unripe-fruit picture that keeps the joke while fixing the part

n1.english: Alright. The tree, I'll let go of. But the picture is the one thing I won't surrender: that scene of a mouth clamped onto a fruit not yet ripe — that stays. "未" comes down to "not yet," doesn't it. So "still sour!" works. This way I shave off not one millimetre of the fun and still get the content right.

nodes.intent: Own that his speed produced the wrong answer, and redesign the challenge so accuracy comes before the race instead of dropping the game.
nodes.attentionTarget: his own rule, which let speed beat checking

nodes.description: The revised card goes back on the wall as the museum's first finished piece — the mouth still mid-bite, 未 in the corner, the ぶひん button glowing on the projector beside it. The wrong stroke is gone; the joke is not.

outcomes.description: A memorable but false kanji mnemonic is corrected against component evidence and rebuilt as a program that keeps its vivid picture while a button reveals the true part 未.
Stasi is introduced through direct visual preference and a vivid card, and revises a false claim against evidence without flattening her expression into a plain correction.
Shin's component decomposition changes the shared card, establishing his stroke-and-reading evidence as a competence the class can ask for when a kanji claim is in doubt.
Tom's fast challenge outruns his own accuracy; the class changes the game to check-then-race rather than punishing him, and he redesigns the rule so speed and accuracy can coexist.
Describe-a-wanted-program-and-button-condition-then-revise-a-changed-plan evidence returns through the registered transfer activity; the story emits no lesson-completion command.
